headline: Markets brace for Fed hike as yields, oil surge higher
body: Sentiment is tilting cautious as investors head into today's Fed decision with the 10-year Treasury yield at its highest level since 2007, having brushed 5% overnight on the back of persistent inflation pressure and oil prices holding above $100 a barrel amid the ongoing Iran conflict. Futures markets have priced in high odds of a quarter-point hike, the first since 2023, which would mark a notable reversal after months of a steady policy stance. Equities pulled back for two straight sessions into the announcement, with the Nasdaq underperforming as higher long-term rates weighed hardest on growth and tech names, though early Wednesday trade showed a tentative bid returning to tech and retail as some investors bet the hike itself could remove uncertainty rather than add to it.

The other thread running through the week is a self-imposed AI slowdown call from several prominent industry leaders, which briefly rattled chipmakers and AI infrastructure names before the broader market mostly shrugged it off by Monday's close. The more durable effect has been a rotation into cybersecurity names, which have caught a bid on expectations that a more cautious AI buildout still means sustained enterprise security spending. Retail chatter has leaned more anxious than greedy this week — overnight social discussion skewed toward loss stories and margin-call anecdotes rather than momentum-chasing, suggesting the mood among individual traders is closer to defensive than euphoric heading into a rate decision that could reset the path for both stocks and bonds.
